THE JOKE IS OVER: WE CAN'T SAY "BEFORE GTA 6" ANYMORE

At midnight tonight in Toronto, the longest-running joke on the internet expires.

Grand Theft Auto VI is out. It unlocked first in New Zealand, where it is already November 19, and it reaches Canada at midnight Eastern. And that means the sentence that defined a generation of waiting — "we got that before GTA 6" — is officially retired. You cannot get anything before GTA 6 anymore. GTA 6 is here. GTA 6 is the thing that arrived.

The wait was real. GTA V launched on September 17, 2013. The sequel took thirteen years, two console generations and three U.S. presidential elections to show up. Fans filled the silence with a joke format so durable it earned its own dictionary entry: take any unlikely event, no matter how big or how stupid, and marvel that it beat Rockstar to the finish line.

The format had scattered early sightings — a 2019 tweet noted the PS5 was announced before GTA 6, and a 2022 Reddit post joked "we really having WW3 before GTA 6" — but it caught fire on July 27, 2023, when TikTok creator Jaden Dunn posted "We got aliens before GTA 6," one day after former intelligence officer David Grusch testified to Congress about UFO programs. The clip passed 260,000 plays, and from there, nothing was safe.

Because the list underneath the joke is genuinely absurd. We got a pandemic before GTA 6. We got the Chicago Cubs winning the World Series, ending a 108-year drought, before GTA 6. We got the entire artificial intelligence era — ChatGPT launched in November 2022 — before GTA 6. We got an American pope, Chicago's own Cardinal Robert Prevost, elected Leo XIV in May 2025, before GTA 6. We got Notre-Dame Cathedral rebuilt and reopened before GTA 6. We got NASA back around the Moon. We got Eminem becoming a grandfather. We got Hollow Knight: Silksong — the other most-delayed game on Earth, a meme in its own right — released in September 2025, before GTA 6. And in October 2026, we got a Tesla Roadster launched off a ramp in Texas, which the internet immediately ruled a flying car. The White House's official account posted its own version of the joke. So did the Department of Labor and U.S. Customs and Border Protection. When the government is doing your meme format, the format owns the culture.

So what replaces it? The game has been out in New Zealand for hours, and the comment sections are already holding auditions.

The first real contender came from Instagram user @21_fsi: "before WW3." It is darker than the original, and it has history on its side — as noted above, WW3 jokes were inside this format as early as 2022. The internet is not inventing a new anxiety. It is promoting an old one.

The second contender: "before the rest of the Epstein files." This one has paperwork. Under the Epstein Files Transparency Act — signed, in a coincidence the internet will enjoy, on November 19, 2025, exactly one year before GTA VI's launch — the Justice Department has released roughly 3.5 million pages. The department says that is everything the law requires. Survivors and lawmakers from both parties say roughly 2.5 to 3 million pages are still being withheld, and this month a federal judge ordered more of the files published, including handwritten FBI interview notes. Nobody can tell you when, or if, the rest arrives. That is exactly what made "before GTA 6" work: a wait with no confirmed end.

The third contender is the connoisseur's pick: "before GTA 6 Online." Here is the part casual fans missed — the game launching tonight is single-player only. Rockstar has not announced an online mode for GTA VI at all: no name, no date, no price. Twitch CEO Dan Clancy told Bloomberg he expects multiplayer in 2027, but that is his expectation, not a Rockstar announcement. In 2013, GTA Online followed GTA V by two weeks. This time there is no timeline to point at, which makes it the truest heir to the throne. The wait starts tonight, and nobody knows how long it runs.

And then there is the final boss, offered up in the same comment threads: "before Jesus comes back." The Second Coming has been expected for roughly two thousand years, which makes Rockstar's thirteen look like a lunch break. Every generation has believed it was living in the last days. If the meme needs a deadline that can never embarrass it by actually arriving, that is the one.

The auditions are not the only madness launch week produced. The game has also become a workplace event: HR firm BambooHR found leave requests for November 19 running nearly 13 percent above comparable Thursdays across more than 3.4 million U.S. employees, and in an IGN poll of 10,400 readers, 42 percent said they had already booked launch day off and another 9 percent planned to call in sick. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick saw it coming months ago, joking that "a lot of people will be calling in sick on November 19." The phenomenon has a name — "GTA flu" — and institutions are responding like it is weather. A school in Norwich, England warned parents not to try it. Britain's National Health Service posted a warning about repetitive strain injury from marathon sessions. KFC Australia staged a mock funeral for the sick day. Logitech simply gave its staff the day off. The U.S. Army's 3rd Infantry Division offered soldiers a four-day pass to play, on one condition: reenlist for at least two years. One employee's leave request, logged by HR firm BrightHR, read in full: "GTA Release — I'll put my notice in if this is denied." A supermarket chain, Aldi Scotland, posted a step-by-step playbook for faking sick, and ESPN's Kyle Brandt went on television and called the day-off crowd "absolute legends."

And because it is 2026, the launch also started a gender war. A rant captioned "GTA6 exposing all the broke and jealous women" has been reposted across Instagram and Facebook, racking up tens of thousands of likes with one argument: women expect men to pay for hair, nails and bills for years, but call a man broke while refusing to spend $100 on the game he waited thirteen years for. The clapback travelled just as far — one viral post, liked more than 120,000 times, asked why anyone who had years to save $100 for this game needs his girlfriend to buy it for him. Around the same argument, girlfriends have been joking about hiding consoles and uninstalling the game before launch, partly in response to a running joke among male players that Lucia, the game's female lead, is their new girlfriend. Strip out the insults flying in both directions and the shape of it is simple: a video game became a relationship test for a week, and everybody performed their side of it for the timeline.

Meanwhile the practical chaos is already here. PlayStation Network sign-in failures hit hours before the Toronto unlock. Fans who cannot wait are deactivating accounts and muting words to dodge spoilers from New Zealand players who are already hours into the story. One viral skit has mothers calling their own children in sick to school — so the mothers can play.

That is the state of play at midnight. Thirteen years of waiting produced a phrase the whole internet shared, and the phrase did what the best memes do: it told the truth. Everything really did happen before GTA 6. A pandemic, a pope, a flying car, the end of the Cubs' curse and the start of the AI age — all of it arrived while one game sat in development.

So the crown passes. Maybe it is WW3. Maybe it is the files. Maybe it is the online mode Rockstar has not even announced, or the oldest deadline of all. Whoever wins, the standard is set: the replacement has to out-wait a pope.

We got the end of the joke before GTA 6. Barely.

— BIA808

text:
Video game enthusiasts' favorite Grand Theft Auto releases its 6th installment after 13 years. 

After a long thirteen-year wait, two major delays, a series of data leaks, and over a decade of development, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6 / GTA VI), eagerly anticipated by video game enthusiasts worldwide, was officially released globally on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Considered one of the most anticipated and highest-cost entertainment productions ever created, this game arrives 13 years after the release of GTA V in 2013.

On November 19, the game gradually opened up to the world as midnight struck in each region's local time, with New Zealand and Eastern Australia being among the first countries to experience it. Pre-downloads for digital copies had begun on November 10. Currently released only for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S console models, it also offers the facility to play via Xbox Cloud Gaming on certain devices. However, Rockstar or Take-Two have not yet officially announced a PC version, and a GamesBeat report, citing anonymous sources, stated that it is likely to be released in the first quarter of 2027. In the American market, the Standard Edition is priced at $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition at $99.99, with pre-orders receiving the Vintage Vice City Pack offer.

This time, the story returns to Rockstar's fictional modern Miami-inspired city, Vice City, and extends across the state of Leonida, inspired by Florida. The narrative revolves around the two main characters, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, within an environment comprising island chains, coastlines, highways, swamps, nightclubs, and the criminal underworld. Jason, who grew up among fraudsters and criminals, left military service under unfavorable circumstances, and now works with drug traffickers on the Leonida islands, desires an easy life, but his life is becoming increasingly difficult. Lucia, the first female protagonist in a mainline GTA game, fought for her family, ended up imprisoned in Leonida, and gained freedom purely by luck. With family ties to Liberty City, she seeks the good life her mother dreamed of. When an easy heist goes wrong, these two are drawn into the darkest side of America's sunniest region, and to survive a criminal conspiracy spanning across Leonida, they must trust each other more than ever. Players can switch between these two characters while playing, and there is also an option to develop an alternative romantic relationship between these criminal partners.

With the lifting of the review embargo a day before its release, on November 18, GTA VI received unprecedented critical acclaim. It achieved a score of 99 on Metacritic, matching the all-time record held by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, released in 1998. No mixed or negative reviews were reported in the initial round, and it also scored 99 on OpenCritic with a 100% recommendation. Leading publications such as IGN, GameSpot, Game Informer, Eurogamer, Forbes, The Washington Post, and The Verge awarded it maximum scores of 10/10 or 5/5, praising its vibrant open world, character relationships, and technical polish.

Analysts also predict this will be the biggest entertainment release in history commercially. According to Sensor Tower's third-party estimates, approximately 15.9 million digital pre-orders were recorded by mid-November, generating revenue between $1.54 billion and $1.7 billion. Between 74% and 75% of these pre-orders were for PlayStation 5, and there was high demand for the more expensive Ultimate Edition. Take-Two, stating that pre-orders are much higher than expected, has projected a financial revenue target of between $8.0 billion and $8.2 billion based on GTA VI. The series has sold approximately 480 million copies overall to date.

This project, developed over more than a decade, was severely impacted by data leaks in 2022 and thereafter. Although initially planned for release in 2025, Rockstar had to postpone it to May 26, 2026, and then to November 19, to achieve the desired quality. While production costs have not been officially disclosed, analysts estimate that production and marketing expenses range from $1 billion to $1.5 billion or more. Rockstar denied some reports that it exceeded $1.5 billion, and Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick only stated that it was a high-cost project.

Scored by the electronic music duo Justice, this game is classified as an adults-only game due to its themes of violence, strong language, sexual content, and crime. A full-fledged GTA Online multiplayer mode has not yet been announced with the release, and official information regarding post-release sales reports, online mode details, and the PC version is expected to be revealed in the coming weeks.

I doubt you will get a response from Jason Kenney, but as a loyal UCP member I would like to offer my opinion on your concerns.

I won’t deny that a segment of the Conservative movement, particularly here in Alberta, has been drawn into Trump’s MAGA rhetoric. Frankly, I find that just as troubling as you do.

But don’t mistake that faction for the entire Conservative movement. Many of us still believe in the principles that traditionally defined Canadian conservatism: fiscal responsibility, individual liberty, democratic institutions, the rule of law and strong international alliances.

We can acknowledge the influence of MAGA without pretending it defines us all. And we can reject separatism without abandoning our Conservative convictions.

Canadian conservatism existed long before Donald Trump came along, and I have every intention of defending those principles long after he’s gone.

America will keep Constitutional Democracy, Not socialism 

Trump supporters may be frustrated by the 2026 midterm results, but they need to examine Trump’s own political choices. During Biden’s presidency, Russia invaded Ukraine while Trump sought a return to the White House. Biden supported Ukraine’s resistance to Putin’s aggression. Trump’s approach to Putin, Xi Jinping, and authoritarian power deserves serious scrutiny. Any allegation of foreign financial influence or coercion requires evidence, but Americans have every right to demand transparency.

Trump’s immigration crackdown and deployment of the National Guard during the Los Angeles protests raised serious questions about civil liberties and executive power. His attempt to overturn the 2020 election, culminating in the January 6 attack on Congress, remains a warning. No president is a king. No political leader stands above the Constitution. Neither socialism nor anti-socialism can justify concentrating power in one person or disabling Congress. Republican voters are not the enemy; authoritarianism is.

The November 3, 2026, midterms gave Democrats control of both chambers of Congress. That result is a democratic judgment, not proof of a conspiracy. America’s future depends on accepting lawful elections, protecting constitutional institutions, and rejecting political intimidation.

We also need economic renewal without absolute isolationism. America can rebuild domestic manufacturing while maintaining international partnerships and helping poorer nations develop. Our Madison and Hamilton reforms offer a constructive direction: protect voting rights, expand opportunity, support small businesses, and strengthen democratic accountability.

America belongs to its citizens—not to Trump, Putin, Xi, Baoxiaoyu’s Xinjiang concentration camp order or any Talism Talism of socialism ideology. We will defend constitutional democracy, liberty, and the rule of law.

text:
SURAH AD-DUKHAN
Number of verses: 59 | Period: Mecca (circa the 7th-8th years of revelation) | Pedagogical order: 85
Subject: Economic Crisis — The Psychology of Historical Warnings
Reference Frame: Qur'an Tafsir Reference Protocol v27 | Foundational Axiom: an-Nisa 136 | Epistemic Limit: Allah knows best.
THE PROTOCOL FRAME AND THE ONTOLOGICAL GROUND
The Foundational Axiom (an-Nisa 136): this analysis proceeds upon the ground of faith in Allah, in His Prophet, in the Book He sent down upon His Prophet, and in the books He sent down before. No interpretation can bring these four pillars to collapse. The analysis of Surah ad-Dukhan, remaining within this ontological frame, aims to bring to light the consciousness of justice, liberty, and responsibility (taqwa) that the revelation offers to humanity.
The Surah's Context of Revelation (0a-0b): Surah ad-Dukhan was sent down in the middle of the Meccan period, in approximately the 7th-8th years of the revelation. According to the report of Ibn Mas'ud, the surah was revealed in the time of famine lived through in Mecca. In the el-Kashshaf (Zamakhshari) it is stated that the surah was revealed in Mecca and that it has 59 verses.
THE FIRST GROUP: AD-DUKHAN 1-6 — THE CLEAR BOOK AND THE BLESSED NIGHT (THE EPISTEMOLOGICAL GROUND OF REVELATION)
The Translation (el-Kashshaf):
1. “Ha, Mim.”
2. “By the Clear Book I swear”
3. “We sent it down upon a blessed night. Surely We are the warners.”
4. “In it every wise affair is separated.”
5. “As a command from Our presence. Surely We are the senders.”
6. “As a mercy from your Lord. Surely He is the Hearer, the Knower.”
Etymological-Semantic Analysis:
“Ha, Mim”: the huruf-i mufassala (the separated letters). According to Zeccac's assessment in the Ma'ani'l-Qur'an, these letters draw attention to the building blocks of the Arabic language and carry the message: “This book is composed of the most basic units of your language; and yet you cannot bring the like of it.” The rational counterpart: the revelation has been built from material the addressee knows; but the structure produced from that material lies beyond the productive capacity of the addressee. This is an epistemological challenge.
“Kitab-i Mubin”: the word “mubin” comes from the root B-Y-N. Zeccac defines this root as “to bring out into the open the side of a thing that remained hidden, to remove ambiguity.” “Mubin” does not only mean “clear”; it means “that which also makes other things clear, that discloses.” Its semantic field: transparency, verifiability, accessibility. In the jahiliyya, knowledge was in the monopoly of the soothsayers and the elite; the attribute “mubin” proclaims the breaking of that monopoly.
“Layla-i mubarak”: the word “night” (layl) in Qur'anic semantics represents the state of darkness, ignorance, and indeterminacy. “Mubarak” comes from the root B-R-K; Zeccac explains it as “the good that is fixed, that strikes root, that continues by increase.” The rational counterpart: the revelation is a process of enlightenment that cleaves the darkness of ignorance. This “night” is not a single calendar night; it is the very process of the revelation's 22 years and 6 months — that is, humanity's passage from darkness to light. The “blessing” expresses the ever-increasing, rooting, good-turning energy of that process.
“Yufrazu kullu emrin hakim”: F-R-Q, coming from the same root as “Furqan,” means “to separate, to distinguish right from falsehood.” “Amr” here means “affair, decree, ordering.” “Hakim” comes from the root H-K-M: “wise, measured, each thing in its place.” Zeccac explains the word “amr” as “decree and governance.” The rational counterpart: in the process of revelation, every wise affair (justice, law, morality, economy) is separated one from another; that is, a system is established in which right is separated from falsehood, justice from oppression, the straight from the crooked. This is not a fatalist “writing of destiny” but the instituting of the systemic laws of the divine pedagogy (Sunnatullah).
“Rahma”: the root R-H-M is connected with the maternal womb; it expresses protective, encompassing, unconditional love and compassion. The revelation is positioned not as an instrument of punishment but as an instrument of mercy (protection, encompassing, compassion).
Rational Analysis:
These six verses establish the epistemological ground of the revelation. The message is this: the source of knowledge is not human speculation but a divine transfer. But this transfer has been given in the language the addressee will understand (Arabic), with the concepts of the age the addressee lived in. The metaphor of “night” represents the ignorance, the tribal wars, and the order of exploitation of seventh-century Arabia. The “blessed night” is the moment at which that order began to be transformed by the revelation. The “separation of every wise affair” is the separating of the legal, moral, and economic system the revelation brought from the jahiliyya confusion.
As required by article 20a of the Protocol (tanZih), the expression “the separation of affairs on that night” cannot be understood as Allah's sitting at a table and writing destiny. This is the symbolic telling of the divine will's operating through universal laws (Sunnatullah).
Structural Sociology:
In the social structure of Mecca, knowledge was in the monopoly of the Quraysh aristocracy (the mala'). The soothsayers, the poets, and the elders controlled knowledge and sustained the social hierarchy through this monopoly of knowledge. The attribute “mubin” (clear, disclosing) is a structural intervention in that knowledge monopoly. Now knowledge comes from a source open, transparent, and verifiable to all. This is the epistemological dimension of the principle of “power and deviation” in article 1a of the Protocol: religion corrects the deviation of power by democratizing knowledge.
Maqasid Detail:
The maqsad of this group is to establish the authority and the epistemological legitimacy of the revelation. The aim is to say to the addressee: “This message has been built from material you know (Arabic); but the structure it produces is beyond your capacity. It comes from a divine source, and its aim is to warn you, to protect you, and to enlighten you.”
In the light of articles 3a (the Common Misunderstanding: the Reduction of Worship to Ritual), 17a (Symbolic Language), and 29 (Structural Sociology) of the Protocol, this is the clearest proof that the Qur'an is not “a book of calendars and nights” but “a manifesto of systemic transformation and the building of civilization.”
To read the “night” as a twelve-hour astronomical span of time, and to hope that the systemic sins committed all through the year (interest, exploitation, the violation of the rights of others, injustice) will be erased in this single night “with tears and ritual,” is wholly contrary to the Qur'anic principles of Taqwa (the Consciousness of Responsibility) and Salih Amal (Systemic Goodness).
1. The Semantic Revolution: “Night” (Layl) and Ontological Darkness (Zulumat)
In Qur'anic terminology “night” and “darkness” (zulumat) are not merely the setting of the sun; they are the symbol of the jahiliyya, of ignorance, of oppression, of superstition, and of the absence of divine guidance (the Furqan) (for example: al-Baqara 257 — from the darknesses to the light).
The “Blessed Night” in ad-Dukhan 3 expresses the moment at which the revelation (the Nur) first burst open within the ontological and sociological darkness (the jahiliyya system) into which seventh-century Arabia and all humanity had sunk — that is, the epoch of the enlightenment revolution that would last some twenty-three years.
This night is “mubarak” (blessed / ever-increasing, striking root and turning to good), because it is not an event that ends in a single night; it is the beginning of the twenty-three-year divine pedagogy that would carry humanity from slavery to freedom, from jahiliyya to justice, from tribalism to universal law.
2. The Sociological Trap of the Traditional Reading
Why the human mind turns to the search for “a single sacred night” can be set upon a rational ground through article 14c of the Protocol (the Neuroscientific Frame):
The Limbic System's Search for the “Shortcut”: the limbic system of the human brain (the center of pleasure, fear, and comfort) flees from an arduous process that requires continual moral effort (taqwa) and a systemic struggle for justice (salih amal). In its place, the idea of “the forgiveness of all sins” through an intense ritual performed one night a year is, for the limbic system, a perfect “psychological mechanism of escape and relief.”
The Preservation of the Status Quo: if a merchant commits fraud in trade all through the year, sustains the order of exploitation with interest (riba), and crushes the weak; but believes that when the “Blessed Night” comes he will be forgiven with weeping — then religion has become a cosmetic instrument that covers over oppression. Article 1c of the Protocol (the True Function of Commands and Prohibitions) objects to this categorically. The Qur'an came down to demolish the superstitions that invent such “magical nights of forgiveness” and make people flee from responsibility (from the day of reckoning).
THE SECOND GROUP: AD-DUKHAN 7-16 — DENIAL, DOUBT, AND THE SYSTEMIC CONSEQUENCE
The Translation (el-Kashshaf):
7. “He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, if you are of certain faith.”
8. “There is no god but Him. He gives life and causes to die. He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.”
9. “No; they are playing in doubt.”
10. “Watch for the day when the heaven brings an evident smoke.”
11. “It will envelop the people. This is a searing punishment.”
12. “Our Lord! Remove the punishment from us. Surely we are believers.”
13. “Where now is their taking of lesson? Yet a clear messenger had come to them.”
14. “Then they turned from him and said, 'A taught madman!'”
15. “We shall remove the punishment a little. Surely you are those who turn back.”
16. “On the day We seize with the great seizure — surely We are the takers of recompense.”
Etymological-Semantic Analysis:
“Shakkin yal'abun”: “shakk” means “doubt, the refusing of faith on account of hesitation”; but the critical word here is “yal'abun” — “they play.” The root L-'-B means “play, amusement, the not taking seriously.” Zeccac explains this usage as “to treat a serious matter as a game.” The semantic message: denial is not an intellectual position but a psychological escape. The addressee's problem is not lack of knowledge but the unwillingness to take responsibility.
“Dukhan”: the root D-H-N means “smoke.” Zeccac defines it as “the substance that rises after burning, that suffocates, that covers the sight.” The symbolic counterpart: smoke carries both a physical meaning (the dust cloud of the famine period, the hallucination hunger produced) and a metaphorical one (a state that covers the truth, that shuts off sight, that suffocates). The rational counterpart: the “blurring of vision” and the “suffocating atmosphere” produced by the system of oppression and denial.
“Muntaqimun”: the root N-Q-M. This word must be read within the frame of article 20a of the Protocol (tanZih). The literal reading of Allah's “taking vengeance” is not a human wrath or rancor. It is an error to confine the abstract/symbolic telling to the concrete/literal. Zeccac explains the root N-Q-M as “to make one live fully the consequences of a thing, to give its return without deficiency.” The rational counterpart: the operating of Sunnatullah (the universal law). It is the collapse of the system of oppression through its own contradictions. The person who opposes gravity prepares his own oppression, his own being crushed beneath the law. Justice, too, is Allah's unchanging law, which cannot be altered. “Vengeance” here is the symbolic expression of the inevitable manifestation of justice. The law of justice operates, and oppression collapses beneath its own weight.
“Al-batshatu'l-kubra”: B-T-S means “to grasp with violence, to seize.” “Kubra” means “the greatest.” This may point to a historical event (Badr or the conquest of Mecca), and likewise expresses in general the inevitable collapse of the system of oppression.
Rational Analysis:
The rational core of this group is this: when the truth comes, to reject it is not an intellectual choice but a psychological escape (“they play in doubt”). This escape is, on the individual plane, “cognitive dissonance,” and on the social plane, the “reflex of preserving the status quo.” If the Meccan aristocracy accepted the egalitarian message the revelation brought, it would lose its economic and social privileges. For this reason it marginalizes the truth with the label “madman.”
The metaphor of “smoke” is the suffocating atmosphere produced by the system of oppression. When a society deviates from justice, “smoke” settles upon it: sight is blurred, breathing grows hard, direction is lost. This operates both on the individual plane (torment of conscience, crisis of meaning) and on the social (chaos, insecurity, ecological destruction).
The expression “Remove the punishment; we shall believe” must be read with the principle of “ran” (neuroplasticity) in article 14e of the Protocol: repeated denial destroys mental flexibility. To say “we shall believe” in the moment of crisis is not a true transformation but the panic reaction of the limbic system. For this reason the expression “you are those who turn back” announces that this reaction is not lasting, that the old habits will return.
Structural Sociology:
The economic structure of Mecca was built upon the trade monopoly of the Quraysh aristocracy. The principles the revelation brought — “justice in measure and weight” (Protocol 30b), “the protection of the orphan's property,” and “infak” — directly threatened this economic structure. The metaphor of “smoke” represents the social suffocation this economic system produced. The gulf between rich and poor enwraps the social fabric like “a suffocating smoke.”
Within the frame of article 29 of the Protocol (Structural Sociology): the message of tawhid is not only a theological revolution but a structural sociological revolution that demolishes tribal/class superiority. The expression “the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them” proclaims that no human power can claim absolute authority (Protocol 10c).
Maqasid Detail:
The maqsad of this group is to expose the psychological and sociological mechanism of denial and to announce the inevitable end of the system of oppression. The word “vengeance” must be read, within the frame of the tanZih principle, as the manifestation of justice. The aim is not to frighten but to warn: “Oppression is not sustainable; it will collapse through its own contradictions.” The human-like understanding of Allah is the product of literal reading. Allah is the possessor of absolute justice and infinite mercy. Vengeance and Allah cannot be thought together. These literal readings that force the symbolic meaning to the point of ascribing slander to Allah must be rejected.
THE THIRD GROUP: AD-DUKHAN 17-33 — THE PHARAOH PARADIGM (HISTORICAL ARCHETYPE AND SYSTEMIC COLLAPSE)
The Translation (el-Kashshaf):
17. “We tested the people of Pharaoh before them. A noble messenger came to them.”
18. “Give me Allah's servants. Surely I am a trustworthy messenger to you.”
19. “Do not grow arrogant against Allah. Surely I bring you a clear proof.”
20. “Surely I have taken refuge in my Lord, who is your Lord also, from your stoning me.”
21. “If you do not believe in me, keep away from me.”
22. “He called upon his Lord: 'These are a criminal people.'”
23. “'Lead My servants forth by night. Surely you will be pursued.'”
24. “'Leave the sea as a dry path. Surely they are a host that will be overtaken.'”
25. “How many gardens and springs they left behind.”
26. “How many crops and noble places.”
27. “How many blessings in which they lived at ease.”
28. “Thus We made another people heirs to them.”
29. “The heaven and the earth did not weep for them; nor were they given respite.”
30. “We delivered the Children of Israel from the abasing punishment.”
31. “From Pharaoh. Surely he was a headstrong criminal.”
32. “We chose them above the worlds upon a knowledge.”
33. “We gave them such signs as in which was a clear trial.”
Etymological-Semantic Analysis:
“Rasulun karim”: the root K-R-M means “precious, honorable, generous.” Zeccac explains “karim” as “one in whom worth and virtue are gathered.” Moses' attribute of “karim” stresses the nobility of the message and the honor of the envoy. Pharaoh, however, weighs the message not by its content but by status; the attribute “karim” reverses this evaluation by status: true worth lies not in power but in the nobility of the message.
“Tariqan yebasa”: Y-B-S means “dry, hard, the water withdrawn.” Zeccac defines “yebes” as “terrain from which the water has withdrawn and hardened.” The symbolic counterpart: stability (dry ground) taking the place of uncertainty (water/sea). Order taking the place of chaos, security the place of fear. The rational counterpart: the passage from the environment of uncertainty the system of oppression created to the environment of security the system of justice creates.
“Mustakbirun”: from the root K-B-R, “to grow great, to hold oneself superior.” Pharaoh's claim “I am your Lord most high” is the historical archetype of the principle of “power and deviation” in article 1a of the Protocol. Power inevitably produces inequality; religion was sent to break this presupposition.
“Ma taraku”: “what they left.” This expression denotes the material accumulation that remained after the collapse of the system of oppression (gardens, springs, crops, places). Zeccac explains “taraku” as “to leave behind, to forsake.” The semantic message: wealth accumulated through oppression loses its meaning with the death of the oppressor; for that wealth was built not upon justice but upon exploitation.
Rational Analysis:
The Pharaoh paradigm is, beyond a historical event, the archetype of the intoxication of power of all times. The rational core is this:
1. The poisoning of power: Pharaoh, saying “give me Allah's servants,” regards human beings as property. This is the inevitable consequence of the absolutizing of power.
2. The collapse of the system: the expression “leave the sea as a dry path” represents the passage from the environment of uncertainty the system of oppression created to the ground of justice. The host of Pharaoh's being “a host that will be overtaken” is the proclamation that the system of oppression will collapse through its own contradictions.
3. The transfer of the inheritance: the expression “We made another people heirs” expresses the passage, after the collapse of the system of oppression, to the system of justice. This is the Sunnatullah principle of article 1f of the Protocol: destruction is not “a sudden execution” but a systemic collapse.
4. “The heaven and the earth did not weep for them”: this expression tells of the incompatibility of the system of oppression with the cosmic order. An unjust system contradicts the universal order (the Mizan); when it collapses, the universe does not “weep” for it — that is, its absence is lived not as a loss but as a correction.
As required by article 20a of the Protocol (tanZih), the expressions of “Allah's taking vengeance” or “the heaven's weeping” cannot be read as the ascribing of human feelings to Allah. These are the symbolic tellings of the operating of the universal law of justice.
Structural Sociology:
The Pharaonic system is the historical example of the principle “the form changed, the essence did not” in article 1e of the Protocol. The relation of the landowner and the peasant takes concrete form in the relation of Pharaoh and the Children of Israel. Today this relation has become the relation of the owners of capital, who hold the means of production, and the wage laborer.
The expression “how many gardens and springs they left” shows the unsustainability of wealth accumulated through oppression. The zakat principle of article 11 of the Protocol, keeping wealth in circulation, prevents the formation of this kind of accumulation (and therewith of the system of oppression).
The expression “We chose the Children of Israel above the worlds” is not an ethnic superiority but a historical assignment of responsibility. The expression “a clear trial” stresses that this choosing is not a privilege but a test.
Maqasid Detail:
The maqsad of this group is to show, through a historical archetype, the inevitable collapse of the system of oppression. The aim is not to give the Meccan aristocracy the message “you too will collapse like Pharaoh,” but to recall a universal law (Sunnatullah): oppression is not sustainable; justice will sooner or later be manifest.
THE FOURTH GROUP: AD-DUKHAN 34-42 — THE SMOKE (DUKHAN) AND THE DENIAL OF THE RESURRECTION
The Translation (el-Kashshaf):
34. “Surely these are saying:”
35. “'There is no death but our first death. We shall not be raised.'”
36. “'Bring our fathers, if you speak the truth.'”
37. “Are these better, or the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them. Surely they were criminals.”
38. “We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.”
39. “We created them only with truth. But most of them do not know.”
40. “Surely the day of separation is the time when they shall all be gathered.”
41. “On that day no friend shall avail a friend, and they shall not be helped.”
42. “Except those upon whom Allah has had mercy. Surely He is the Mighty, the Merciful.”
Etymological-Semantic Analysis:
“Al-mawtatatu'l-ula”: “the first death.” The root M-W-T means “death, the ending of life.” “Ula” means “first.” The rational counterpart: biological death in this world. The deniers' claim is this: “We die once, and there is nothing after.” This claim removes the consciousness of responsibility (taqwa); for if there is no reckoning, the demand for justice also becomes meaningless.
“La'b”: “play.” The root L-'-B is the same root as the “yal'abun” of verse 9. The expression “We did not create the heavens and the earth in play” proclaims that the universe carries a purpose, that it is not a meaningless chaos. The rational counterpart: the universe is teleological (purposeful); human life likewise is not a meaningless game but a process bearing responsibility.
“Yawmu'l-fasl”: F-S-L means “to separate, to give a definitive judgment.” “The day of separation” expresses the day on which right will be separated from falsehood, justice from oppression, the straight from the crooked, definitively. The rational counterpart: the moment at which the consequences of actions appear in full, when no ambiguity remains.
“Mawla”: the root W-L-Y means “friend, protector, possessor.” The expression “no friend shall avail a friend” expresses that worldly relations (ties of blood, class solidarity, political alliance) will lose their validity on that day. The rational counterpart: responsibility is individual; no social belonging can transfer a person's reckoning to another.
Rational Analysis:
The rational core of this group is to expose the psychology behind the denial of the resurrection. The claim “there is no death but our first death” in truth means “I do not want to give account.” For if there is resurrection and reckoning, oppression is not sustainable; justice will sooner or later be manifest.
The expression “We did not create the heavens and the earth in play” rejects the materialist and nihilist worldview. The universe is not “an amusement park” but a field of responsibility. This is connected with the liberty principle of article 1b of the Protocol: liberty without responsibility is meaningless; responsibility without reckoning is meaningless.
The reference to “the people of Tubba'” is a historical warning: there were powerful peoples before you; they too were criminals and were destroyed. This shows the historical continuity of Sunnatullah (the universal law).
Structural Sociology:
The expression “no friend shall avail a friend” proclaims that tribal solidarity (asabiyya) will lose its validity on that day. In jahiliyya society the individual existed through his tribe; the tribal chief assumed the individual's reckoning. The revelation breaks this structure: responsibility is individual; no social belonging can take over the individual's reckoning before Allah. This is the individual dimension of the structural sociological revolution of article 29 of the Protocol.

text:
When we were taking about the parable of the talents (coins) I thought of this talk from Elder Bednar:

“The scriptures highlight instructive uses of the word endure. For example, the Lord declared to the Nephites, “Look unto me, and endure to the end, and ye shall live; for unto him that endureth to the end will I give eternal life.”

And the Savior revealed through the Prophet Joseph Smith that “if you keep my commandments and endure to the end you shall have eternal life, which gift is the greatest of all the gifts of God.”

“I pray for the assistance of the Holy Ghost as we consider a higher and holier understanding of what it means to endure to the end as lifelong disciples of the Lord Jesus Christ.

The Savior’s restored gospel invites us to be spiritually transformed—not merely to improve our behavior. As we align our character, desires, actions, and what we truly love more closely with God’s will, the Savior can bring about a comprehensive and complete change in us.

As we strive to put off the natural man and become Saints through the Savior’s Atonement, we are to “come unto [Him],” be “born again,” bind ourselves to the Father and the Son through sacred covenants and ordinances, pledge our willingness to take upon us the Savior’s name, “receive a fulness of the Holy Ghost,” experience a “mighty change [of] heart,” and serve the Lord with all our “heart, might, mind and strength.” We are to become new creatures in Christ.

This mighty spiritual change is possible only “through the merits, … mercy, and grace of the Holy Messiah.” As mortal beings, we are in absolute and never-ending need of Heavenly Father’s and the Savior’s help to realize our eternal destiny.

Mormon testified that “charity is the pure love of Christ” and “the greatest of all” spiritual gifts. Significantly, the word endure is used in the scriptures to define and describe charity.

For example, “charity … endureth forever,” “suffereth long, … seeketh not her own, … beareth all things, … endureth all things.” And, as you sisters know well, “charity never faileth.”

Mormon also taught that “whoso is found possessed of [the spiritual gift of charity] at the last day, it shall be well with him.” Note the double meaning of the word of in this verse. We can possess charity, but ultimately charity should possess us.

As we are blessed to receive this supernal gift, a transformation occurs in our spiritual nature and character. Being “possessed” of the spiritual gift of charity refers in part to the spiritual development and progress that are the overarching purposes of the Savior’s gospel.

Caeden Moody: A Class of 2027 Cornerback College Coaches Should Watch
SELMA, AL — As college football programs search for defensive backs who combine athleticism, speed, and competitive ability, Selma High School cornerback Caeden Moody is a prospect deserving further evaluation.
The Class of 2027 defensive back stands 5’10”, weighs 170 pounds, and has demonstrated measurable athletic ability, including a 4.58-second 40-yard dash, 34-inch vertical jump, and 4.44-second shuttle.
Moody also maintains a 3.3 GPA, adding an academic component to his recruiting profile.
Athleticism and Defensive Potential
Cornerback is one of football’s most demanding defensive positions. Players must react quickly, recognize offensive concepts, change direction, and remain disciplined in coverage.
Moody’s athletic testing provides a foundation for continued development.
His 4.58-second 40-yard dash demonstrates his recorded straight-line speed, while his 34-inch vertical jump offers a measurable indicator of lower-body explosiveness. His 4.44-second shuttle provides another useful measure of change-of-direction performance.
Together, these results give college coaches measurable information to consider alongside game film.

The staff also highlights his ability to locate and make plays on the football.

A cornerback who can support the run game and demonstrate ball awareness gives a defensive coordinator additional qualities to evaluate.

His strengths include his ability to pull, move into open space, identify blocking assignments, and engage defenders beyond the line of scrimmage.
These qualities are particularly valuable for an offensive guard in a running scheme that requires movement, coordination, and effective second-level blocking.
The scouting staff describes Vinson as an athletic offensive lineman who understands where he needs to be on the field.

text:
🏈 NFL Week 11 Matchup Review

Indianapolis Colts (3-7) at Houston Texans (3-6)
Line: Texans (-12.5)
Total: 44

Summary: Thursday Night Football features an AFC South rematch where a desperate Texans squad looks to avenge a narrow 19-17 Week 3 road loss against a Colts team leaning heavily on its ground game.

Colts:

+ Ground efficiency has kept them competitive in tight spots, bolstered by a strong interior rushing scheme that helped them survive Miami 24-22 in Week 10.

- Own the worst seasonal point differential in the AFC South (-63), conceding an average of 27.1 points per game.

Texans:

+ Generate strong aerial production with a +0.130 offensive passing EPA per play and a deep 9.57 Average Depth of Target (ADoT).

- Remain winless at home (0-4) this season and suffer from an inefficient ground attack posting a -0.131 rushing EPA per play.

Lean: Laying Texans -12.5 is heavily supported by Houston's explosive passing advantage against a leaky Indianapolis secondary. While the Colts pulled off a two-point upset in Week 3, Indianapolis holds a brutal 1-4 road record and is playing on a short week with a compromised passing floor. Houston's vertical scheme (2,469 passing yards) has the potential here to separate early against a defense allowing over 27 points per game, making the double-digit spread a worthwhile play.

Miami Dolphins (1-8) at Buffalo Bills (8-1)
Line: Bills (-16.5)
Total: 45

Summary: An AFC East mismatch pits the league's highest-scoring offense against a rebuilding Miami roster starting a rookie quarterback on the road.

Dolphins:

+ Showed structural grit in Week 10 by holding Indianapolis to just 279 total yards and 4.7 yards per play in a narrow two-point loss.

- Rank dead last in the NFL in defensive EPA per play (+0.110), struggling consistently to prevent explosive plays.

Bills:

+ Lead the entire NFL in offensive efficiency, ranking 1st in offensive EPA per play (+0.178), passing EPA per play (+0.282), and scoring at 31.9 points per game.

- Pass defense shows occasional vulnerability when playing with large leads, yielding a +0.235 defensive passing EPA per play.

Lean: Backing Bills -16.5 is justified by one of the largest analytical mismatches of the 2026 season. Buffalo enters Week 11 riding a five-game winning streak with a +88 point differential, while Miami is forced to navigate a hostile Highmark Stadium environment with rookie Kyle McCord under center. Given Buffalo's league-leading 20 rushing touchdowns and Miami's bottom-tier defensive metrics, the Bills should comfortably dictate tempo and clear the massive number.

Baltimore Ravens (4-6) at Carolina Panthers (4-5)
Line: Panthers (-2.5)
Total: 44

Summary: A surging Panthers squad that just claimed sole possession of first place in the NFC South hosts a reeling Ravens team trapped in a five-game losing streak.

Ravens:

+ Quarterback Jacoby Brissett provided an immediate vertical spark in his Week 10 debut, throwing for a team season-high 340 yards.

- Have dropped five straight games and enter with a -50 point differential after converting just two touchdowns on 12 drives against the Chargers.

Panthers:

+ Possess an elite run-stopping front that has surrendered an NFL-low 2.59 yards per carry since Week 8.

- Lead the NFL in self-inflicted mistakes with a league-worst 787 penalty yards, including a franchise-record 17 flags for 152 yards in Week 10.

Lean: Taking Panthers -2.5 aligns directly with both current trench dominance and betting market movement. Carolina's front seven just bottled up New Orleans and is uniquely equipped to neutralize Derrick Henry, who was held to 10 yards on 10 carries on Monday night. With Baltimore traveling on a short week after a crushing home defeat to a previously winless team, laying less than a field goal with the NFC South leaders offers tremendous value.

New Orleans Saints (3-7) at Chicago Bears (7-2)
Line: Bears (-11.5)
Total: 48

Summary: A red-hot Bears team riding a four-game winning streak welcomes a struggling Saints offense into Soldier Field.

Saints:

+ Field an aggressive offensive tempo that averages 65.8 plays per game, keeping opposing defenses on the field.

- Suffer from severe defensive inefficiency, allowing a 49.6% opponent success rate and a +0.074 defensive EPA per play.

Bears:

+ Dominate situational volume by leading the NFL with 70.6 offensive plays per game while limiting opponents to just 20.4 points per contest.

- Remain winless inside their own division (0-2) despite holding a 7-2 overall record and a +57 point differential.

Lean: Taking Saints +11.5 is a strong contrarian play supported by betting market totals and Chicago's tendency to play close games. While Chicago boasts a 4-1 home record, the Bears' offense generates a modest +0.052 EPA per play and relies heavily on high play volume rather than explosive downfield strikes. Computer simulations and market movement suggest New Orleans can generate enough garbage-time yardage against a Bears defense allowing 5.94 yards per play to perhaps slip inside the 11.5-point hook.

Tennessee Titans (1-8) at Dallas Cowboys (4-6)
Line: Cowboys (-7.5/8)
Total: 55

Summary: Two teams with bottom-tier defenses collide in Arlington in a matchup projected to produce the highest point total of the Week 11 slate.

Titans:

+ Play with solid road resilience compared to their winless home mark (0-5), earning their lone victory away from Nashville.

- Own a -72 point differential and have surrendered 40 or more points in back-to-back games following a trade deadline defensive teardown.

Cowboys:

+ Rank 5th in the NFL in scoring at 28.6 points per game and boast a 49.5% offensive success rate after hanging 40 points on San Francisco.

- Yield a massive 6.14 yards per play and 28.2 points per game defensively, completely wasting top-tier offensive outputs.

Lean: Laying Cowboys -7.5 is heavily backed by historical cross-conference trends and a massive disparity in offensive firepower. Tennessee is just 3-8-1 (27%) against the spread over its last 12 games against NFC opponents, whereas Dallas has covered at a 67% clip (4-2 ATS) in its last six against the AFC. Against a hollowed-out Titans secondary that just gave up 40 points to Jacksonville, Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens should be able clear the touchdown margin. The question remains whether the Dallas defense can do its part.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) at Detroit Lions (7-2)
Line: Lions (- 7)
Total: 44

Summary: Coming off their bye week, the Buccaneers travel to Ford Field to test their opportunistic defense against an undefeated-at-home Lions powerhouse.

Buccaneers:

+ Lead the entire NFL in both total takeaways and interceptions while boasting the league's 2nd-best defensive EPA per play (-0.160).

- Face major quarterback uncertainty entering the week as Baker Mayfield manages a new injury, forcing roster shuffles behind center.

Lions:

+ Hold a spotless 5-0 record at Ford Field and rank 3rd in the NFL in offensive EPA per play (+0.130).

- Defensive front must adjust to replacing star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson's production while yielding a +0.130 defensive EPA per play.

Lean: Backing Lions -7 capitalizes on Tampa Bay's severe quarterback instability and Detroit's unmatched home dominance. While Tampa Bay's defense excels at generating turnovers, Detroit has protected the football at an elite level (1.31% interception rate) and averages 5.98 yards per play on turf. Facing a Buccaneers offense potentially led by backup Jalon Daniels, Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs should easily pull away in the second half.

Arizona Cardinals (3-7) at Kansas City Chiefs (7-2)
Line: Chiefs (- 16)
Total: 41

Summary: A reeling Cardinals team starting a rookie quarterback enters Arrowhead Stadium as massive underdogs against a surging Chiefs squad.

Cardinals:

+ Maintain a respectable 45.4% offensive success rate on early downs despite recent roster attrition.

- Suffered a catastrophic Week 10 collapse against the Rams, managing just 123 total yards, six first downs, and an NFL-worst -0.62 EPA per play in rookie Carson Beck's debut.

Chiefs:

+ Rank 2nd in the AFC in scoring defense at 17.3 points allowed per game and hold an undefeated 4-0 home record with a +81 point differential.

- Operate a compressed vertical passing scheme with a 6.15 Average Depth of Target (ADoT), relying heavily on methodical drives.

Lean: Laying Chiefs -16 is a justified position given the extreme processing gap between Steve Spagnuolo's defense and a rookie quarterback making his second career start. Arizona went 0-for-6 on third downs and held the ball for under 18 minutes last week, demonstrating zero schematic answers without Gardner Minshew. Kansas City just cruised to a 35-13 road win in Atlanta (7.3 yards per play) and possesses the exact defensive discipline to pitch a near-shutout at Arrowhead.

Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-7)
Line: Eagles (+ 4.5)
Total: 37.5

Summary: The Battle of Pennsylvania features a physical Steelers squad looking to rebound from a divisional loss against an Eagles team trapped in a seven-game losing streak.

Steelers:

+ Field one of the league's premier scoring defenses, allowing just 20.2 points per game and -0.036 defensive EPA per play.

- Aerial attack lacks efficiency, posting a negative passing EPA per play (-0.039) after managing just 18 points in Cincinnati.

Eagles:

+ Come off a Week 10 bye with extra preparation time to fix their red-zone execution.

- Carry the worst point differential in the NFC (-73), averaging a league-low 16.4 points per game during a seven-game skid.

Lean: Backing Steelers -4.5 is strongly supported by Philadelphia's complete offensive collapse and historical rivalry trends. Pittsburgh has won two straight meetings against its in-state rival and holds a 3-0 non-conference record this season. Even with Philadelphia coming off a bye, an offense scoring just 148 total points across nine games lacks the structural efficiency to keep pace with a Steelers defense that ranks 6th in defensive EPA per play.

New York Jets (2-8) at Los Angeles Chargers (1-8)
Line: Chargers (-3)
Total: 42

Summary: Two struggling AFC franchises meet at SoFi Stadium after the Chargers finally snapped their season-opening losing streak on Monday night.

Jets:

+ Generate a solid +0.098 offensive passing EPA per play while maintaining a 45.41% overall offensive success rate.

- Have lost five consecutive games and sit at 0-3 in divisional play with a -60 point differential.

Chargers:

+ Justin Herbert delivered an efficient, mistake-free performance in Week 10 to secure a 23-20 upset victory in Baltimore.

- Own the worst point differential in the entire NFL (-95) and remain winless at SoFi Stadium (0-4).

Lean: Taking Jets +3 offers clear betting value in a matchup between two sub-.250 teams separated by less than a game in the standings. The Chargers are playing on a short week after traveling back from a physical Monday Night Football win in Baltimore, creating a classic emotional letdown spot. With Los Angeles still winless at home and averaging just 16.0 points per game on the season, grabbing the 3 points  with a Jets offense that outgained Buffalo in total yards last week (376) could be the sharpest angle.

Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) at Denver Broncos (7-2)
Line: Broncos (- 10.5)
Total: 40

Summary: Returning from their bye week, the AFC West co-leader Broncos host a Raiders squad transitioning to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.

Raiders:

+ Rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza flashed legitimate vertical poise in his Week 10 debut, helping Las Vegas maintain a +0.153 passing EPA per play.

- Field the league's most broken ground game (-0.212 rushing EPA per play) paired with a porous defense allowing 28.9 points per game.

Broncos:

+ Enter on a five-game winning streak with an undefeated 4-0 home record and a stingy defense allowing just 20.7 points per game.

- Offensive efficiency lags behind their record, ranking near the bottom of contenders with a -0.027 offensive EPA per play and a 38.6% success rate.

Lean: Taking Raiders +10.5 is a strong situational play built on Denver's low-scoring offensive profile and post-bye rust. While Denver's defense is elite (-0.036 defensive EPA per play), the Broncos' offense averages just 22.0 points per game and struggles to generate explosive separation (6.12 ADoT), making it difficult for them to pull away by double digits. With the game total sitting at a low 40, getting nearly over ten points with a Raiders passing attack that averages 25.1 points per game provides a massive cushion.

Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) at New York Giants (5-3-1)
Line: Giants (+6)
Total: 46.5

Summary: A high-flying Jaguars team riding a three-game winning streak travels to MetLife Stadium to face an NFC East leader trying to rebound from a Thursday night loss.

Jaguars:

+ Boast the best point differential in the NFL (+125), scoring 29.9 points per game while holding opponents to a league-low 16.0 points per contest.

- Ground efficiency remains slightly below average at -0.031 rushing EPA per play, leaning heavily on Trevor Lawrence's arm.

Giants:

+ Outgained Washington 400 to 342 in total yards during Week 10 while averaging a strong 6.3 yards per play.

- Have yet to beat a single team with a winning record in 2026 and are navigating backup quarterback J.J. McCarthy against a top-tier defense.

Lean: Laying Jaguars -6 is backed by an overwhelming statistical mismatch and New York's inability to compete against upper-echelon opponents. Jacksonville ranks 3rd in the NFL in defensive EPA per play (-0.109) and 4th in offensive EPA per play (+0.11), fresh off dropping 40 points in Nashville. With the Giants losing their only prior test against a winning team by 22 points (28-6 to the Rams), Jacksonville's balanced dominance has solid potential to clear the sub-touchdown spread.

Minnesota Vikings (7-2) at San Francisco 49ers (8-1) (Mexico City)
Line: 49ers (-3)
Total: 46.5

Minnesota Vikings (7-2) at San Francisco 49ers (8-1) (Mexico City)

Summary: The NFL's final international game of 2026 takes place at high altitude in Mexico City between two NFC heavyweights.

Vikings:

+ Field the NFL's top-ranked defense in both EPA per play (-0.168) and points allowed (14.0 PPG), fresh off a 30-10 road rout of Green Bay.

- Offensive efficiency remains reliant on conservative game scripts, posting a modest +0.02 EPA per play in Week 10 despite the lopsided score.

49ers:

+ Lead the NFC at 8-1 while ranking 1st in the NFL in offensive success rate (52.5%) and yards per play (6.66) after scoring 46 points in Dallas.

- Defensive passing unit yielded 40 points to the Cowboys in Week 10, showing vulnerability against high-volume aerial attacks.

Lean: Taking Vikings +3 is the position in a neutral-site altitude game between two 7+ win contenders. Kirk Cousins has stabilized Minnesota's offense in his return last week (52% offensive success rate, zero turnovers), giving the league's No. 1 scoring defense the exact complementary support it lacked. Getting the three points against a 49ers defense that just surrendered 40 points makes Minnesota an ideal underdog play.

Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) at Washington Commanders (3-5-1)
Line: Commanders + 6.5
Total: 54

Summary: Monday Night Football features red-hot Joe Burrow and the AFC North-leading Bengals visiting a Commanders squad coming off a Thursday night divisional upset.

Bengals:

+ Riding a five-game winning streak behind Joe Burrow's elite +0.27 passing EPA per play (2,795 yards, 27 TDs) and a +85 point differential.

- Rushing attack ranks near the bottom of the league at -0.12 EPA per rush, generating just 763 total yards on the ground.

Commanders:

+ Executed a 58% offensive success rate and converted 50% of third downs (7-for-14) in their Week 10 road win over the Giants.

- Defense struggles mightily against the pass, surrendering a +0.133 defensive passing EPA per play and 24.8 points per game.

Lean: Laying Bengals -6.5 is heavily supported by Cincinnati's unstoppable aerial efficiency against one of the NFC's most porous secondaries. Even with Washington enjoying extra rest following Thursday Night Football, the Commanders' pass defense (+0.133 EPA/pass) has no schematic answer for a Bengals offense averaging 30.9 points per game and 6.24 yards per play. Cincinnati is 4-1 on the road this season and should exploit Washington's back-end vulnerabilities to cover under a touchdown.

text:
THE SAGE

FORTRESS OF GOLD

The Grand, Yet Often Quite Fatal Illusion of Affluence

At the zenith of his spectacular career, Gianni Versace’s creations strutted the catwalks of the world’s glamor capitals with uncontroverted supremacy. He was the undisputed king of global fashion. His was not merely substantial wealth; it was also one that spoke into the drama of ostentatious theatre. He was so flush with cash that he bought the hotel next door to his Miami Beach mansion for eight million dollars and tore it down just to construct a swimming pool lined with 24-karat gold.

He was the visionary designer who draped Princess Diana of Wales, Madonna, and the era's top supermodels in rarely before seen sartorial elegance and panache. He spoke of beauty with the effortless authority of a man who claimed exclusive ownership of it. Sadly, it was at the height of this gilded reign that the most celebrated designer on Earth was gunned down on his own front steps by a fugitive who would take his own life eight days later.

For two decades, Versace had built an empire around the spectacle of visibility. Everything, from his opulent runway shows and star-studded galas to his sprawling villa, served as a monument to glamor. His mansion was nothing short of a fortress of affluence, complete with heavy wrought-iron gates and towering walls designed to separate him from the rest of the world. 

Yet every barrier he raised and every lock he fastened faced outward toward admiring crowds and the paparazzi. None of his defenses were prepared for the stranger who arrived, not as a grand adversary, but as an unremarkable shadow that emerged unobtrusively from the crowd.

On the morning of July 15, 1997, Versace followed his usual, mundane routine. He ambled over to a neighborhood café, bought some magazines, and returned home. As he bent to unlock his front gate, a young man in a white cap stepped out of the sunlight behind him and fired two shots into the back of his head.

Tragically, by 9:15 a.m., the king of fashion lay dead on his own threshold. Remarkably, the assassin did not even run away; he simply turned and strolled down Ocean Drive at an easy pace, blending among sunbathers and café patrons as though nothing had happened. 

Versace was the fifth victim of a three-month, cross-country killing spree. Before arriving Miami, the gunman had previously murdered a close friend, a former lover, a Chicago real estate developer, and a stranger whose truck he stole. The crimes appeared so erratic that the FBI could not decipher his motive. For eight days, he hid on a houseboat until the police closed in and he turned the gun on himself, taking his motives with him to the grave.

Versace’s senseless end was also the tragic loss of one of the most brilliant creative minds on Earth. Yet, the enduring lesson here has nothing to do with high fashion, but everything to do with the vanity of affluence. We often treat wealth as an armor, believing enough money can purchase immunity from chaos, tragedy, and the capricious nature of fate. Versace spent millions erecting a golden sanctuary to separate himself from the world, yet all his fortune could not buy him a single second of warning. 

Prestige and luxury offer a seductive illusion of control, lulling us into guarding against grand rivals while overlooking our shared human fragility. Ultimately, no fortress of gold can outbuild mortality, and the danger we actually face, even in our common, everyday experience, is rarely the threat we brace ourselves against; that mortal danger is often merely that faceless force we never bothered to give a second glance. 

Yomi Garnett MD

Published: 10 October 1996
Russian documents Set out 'tectonic weapon' research
Carl Levitin

Moscow. The first official details have emerged in Moscow of ambitious research into 'tectonic warfare' carried out by the former Soviet Union and subsequently by the government of Russia, and involving atte mpts to stimulate 'artificial' earthquakes as weapons of destruction. According to documents obtained by the newspaper Moscow News, two research programmes, the first known as ' Mercury ' and the second as ' Volcano', were aimed at creating new earthquake epicentres by using underground nuclear explosions . Geophysicists are aware that impending earthquakes may be triggered by underground nuclear explosions . But Western geophysicists remain sceptical about tectonic warfare and have all but abandoned research after two unsuccessful phases of activity in the 1960s and 1980s, says Roger Clark, a lecturer in geophysics at the University of Leeds. Clark is not at all surprised that th e Russians tried to create earthquakes and control their location electromagnetically, however. "This sort of science is very much part of their heritage. We don't think it is impossible, or wrong , but past experience suggests it is very, very unlikely. "

The programme , which was secretly launched by the Communist rulers of the former Soviet Union in 1987, and has been unofficially known to Western geophysicists for several years, is now believed to have been abandoned. It would certainly contravene the terms of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, which Russia signed at the United Nations in Geneva last month . The Mercury project was launched in the former Soviet republic of Azerbaijan, but came to a halt when the republic became independent. It was superseded by the Volcano project. Three underground nuclear tests are believed to have taken place at sites in Kyrgyzstan.

According to the documents, the Mercury project was launched by a secret decree of the Central Committee of the Communist Party and the Council of Ministers of the Soviet Union. Defense Primer: Directed-Energy Weapons
Both the 2022 National Defense Strategy and the House Armed Services Committee’s bipartisan Future of Defense Task Force Report have identified directed energy as a technology that could have a significant impact on U.S. national security in the years to come. As the Department of Defense (DOD) continues to invest in directed-energy (DE) weapons, Congress may consider implications for defense authorizations, appropriations, and oversight. Overview DOD defines DE weapons as those using concentrated electromagnetic energy, rather than kinetic energy, to “incapacitate, damage, disable, or destroy enemy equipment, facilities, and/or personnel.” DE weapons include high-energy lasers (HEL) and high-powered microwave (HPM) weapons; other DE weapons, such as particle beam weapons, are outside the scope of this In Focus. HELs might be used by ground forces in short-range air defense (SHORAD), counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS), or counter-rocket, artillery, and mortar (C-RAM) missions. The weapons might be used to “dazzle” (i.e., temporarily disable) or damage satellites and sensors. This could in turn interfere with intelligence-gathering operations; military cmmunications; and positioning, navigation, and timing systems used for weapons targeting. In addition, HELs could theoretically provide options for boost-phase missile intercept, given their speed-of-light travel time; however, experts disagree on the affordability, technological feasibility, and utility of this application. In general, HELs might offer lower costs per shot and— assuming access to a sufficient power supply—deeper magazines compared with traditional munitions. (Although a number of different types of HELs exist, many of the United States’ current programs are solid state lasers, which are fueled by electrical power. As a result, the cost per shot is equivalent to the cost of the electrical power required to fire the shot.) This could in turn produce a favorable cost exchange ratio for the defender, whose marginal costs would be significantly lower than those of the aggressor.

Poojaa Precision Engineering | H1 FY27 Concall Updates: 

1/
Poojaa Precision is transitioning from a conventional aluminium casting manufacturer into an integrated precision engineering partner.

2/ H1 FY27:
• Revenue: 210 Cr (+68%)
• EBITDA: 40 Cr (+73%)
• PAT: 25 Cr (+88%)
• EBITDA margin: 19%
• PAT margin: 12%

3/Order Book & Growth Visibility
• Order book: 1,180 Cr
• Auto: 52%
• Non-auto: 48%
• Annual RFQs: 2,000 Cr+
• Historical strike rate: 8–10%
• New business addition: 160–180 Cr annually
Management expects ~50% revenue growth in FY27, followed by 30–35% CAGR.
Target: 1,000 Cr revenue by FY30.

4/Capex: 
Current capacity:
• Melting: 13,800 MT
• Casting & finishing: 6,000 MT

FY28 target:
• Melting: 28,800 MT
• Casting & finishing: 12,600 MT
Capacity nearly doubles.💡
Initial incremental capacity is operational. Remaining machine installation is expected by September 2027.
Mgmt believes the planned capacity is sufficient for 1,000 Cr revenue.

5/The Biggest Structural Change💡

Non-auto is becoming an important growth engine.
H1 FY27:
• Non-auto revenue: 53 Cr, +194% YoY.
• Mgmt cited power & energy as the largest non-auto segment.
• Agriculture is second, healthcare third.
• Defence expected to add over the next two years.📝

Long-term ambition: 50:50 auto and non-auto mix.
Importantly, mgmt indicated that non-auto contributed 60% of the reported margin contribution despite a lower revenue share.

6/ Margin Outlook
EBITDA margin reached 19%.
Important points to note👉
• Gross margin declined from 59% to 53%, partly due to a shift from smaller 1–9 kg components to larger 50–80 kg components.
• Aluminium cost increases are fully passed on to customers.
• Unit 3 fixed costs are already absorbed.
• Higher non-auto contribution and direct exports could support margins.

Mgmt expects PAT margins to improve with operating leverage and lower finance costs.

7/Business Model & Competitive Positioning💡

Poojaa offers an integrated manufacturing ecosystem:
• Co-engineering and design
• In-house tooling and simulation
• GDC, LPDC and HPDC casting
• Multi-axis CNC machining
• Testing and quality assurance

Process mix:
GDC: 70%
LPDC: 25%
HPDC: 5%
Customer base increased from 39 in FY24 to 58 in H1 FY27.

8/Power, Energy & Export Opportunity

Mgmt is positioning itself across multiple Fortune 500 customers in the power distribution ecosystem.
Rather than depending on one tender winner, it wants to be an approved supplier across multiple players.
It also aims to leverage their global relationships to expand exports.

Mgmt discussed increasing certain supply quantities from ~100 to 1,000+ units.

A potentially important scaling opportunity.

9/Balance Sheet: 

• Inventory: 60 Cr, including 20 Cr of die stock.
• Die development cycle: 6–9 months.
• Normal operating cycle: approximately one month.
• Debt-to-equity: 0.08x.
• Mgmt plans to repay the entire loan by Q2.
• 40% primary alloy sourcing; 60% customer-validated ready-made alloys.
Selective outsourcing of non-critical machining and surface treatment helps optimise internal capacity.

10/Long-Term Optionality 

HAL prototype approval and Indian Air Force vendor approval received.
Aluminium-magnesium alloys and magnesium casting are under exploration. Aerospace commercialisation may take at least four years and require a separate Unit 4 facility.

Key risks to track:❗
• Capacity commissioning and utilisation.
• Working capital and cash conversion.
• Customer concentration.
• Order book execution.
• Margin sustainability.
• Non-auto diversification.

Crux:
Poojaa is not merely betting on aluminium casting volumes.

It is building an integrated precision engineering platform, expanding into higher-value components and diversifying beyond automotive.

1,000 Cr FY30 ambition is interesting. The real monitorables are execution, cash flows and sustainable margins.

The next 4 quarters will be critical in validating this growth story.

A martyr (Greek: μάρτυς, mártys, 'witness' stem μαρτυρ-, martyr-) is someone who suffers persecution and death for advocating, renouncing, or refusing to renounce or advocate, a religious belief or other cause as demanded by an external party. In colloquial usage, the term can also refer to any person who suffers a significant consequence in protest or support of a cause.

In the martyrdom narrative of the remembering community, this refusal to comply with the presented demands results in the punishment or execution of an individual by an oppressor. Accordingly, the status of the 'martyr' can be considered a posthumous title as a reward for those who are considered worthy of the concept of martyrdom by the living, regardless of any attempts by the deceased to control how they will be remembered in advance.[1] Insofar, the martyr is a relational figure of a society's boundary work that is produced by collective memory.[2] Originally applied only to those who suffered for their religious beliefs, the term has come to be used in connection with people killed for a political cause.

Most martyrs are considered holy or are respected by their followers, becoming symbols of exceptional leadership and heroism in the face of difficult circumstances. Martyrs play significant roles in religions. Similarly, martyrs have had notable effects in secular life, including such figures as Socrates, among other political and cultural examples.

Meaning
In its original meaning, the word martyr, meaning witness, was used in the secular sphere as well as in the New Testament of the Bible.[4] The process of bearing witness was not intended to lead to the death of the witness, although it is known from ancient writers (e.g., Josephus) and from the New Testament that witnesses often died for their testimonies.

During the early Christian centuries, the term acquired the extended meaning of believers who are called to witness for their religious belief, and on account of this witness, endure suffering or death. The term, in this later sense, entered the English language as a loanword. The death of a martyr or the value attributed to it is called martyrdom.

The early Christians who first began to use the term martyr in its new sense saw Jesus as the first and greatest martyr, on account of his crucifixion.[5][6][7] The early Christians appear to have seen Jesus as the archetypal martyr.[8]: 217–229 

The word martyr is used in English to describe a wide variety of people. However, the following table presents a general outline of common features present in stereotypical martyrdoms.

A female martyr may rarely be referred to as a martyress.[9][10]

Martyrdom in the Middle East
In contemporary Middle Eastern cultures, the term for 'martyr' (Arabic shahid) has more uses than the English word 'martyr'.[11]: 198 

While the term can be narrowly used for a person who is killed because of their religion, it is more generally used to mean a person who died a violent death. Thus it can arguably mean a general 'victim'.[12]

A person is a martyr if they were killed because of their identity, because of natural disasters like earthquakes,[13] or while performing relief or health care work. For example, İbrahim Bilgen was killed by Israel in the 2010 Gaza flotilla raid. Because he died as a humanitarian activist, he is called a martyr by Al-Jazeera.[14]

Martyrdom is also tied with nationalism, because a martyr can be a person who died in the context of national struggle.[15] For example, in Beirut, Martyrs' Square is a public square that's dedicated to Lebanese nationalists who were executed by the Ottomans.

In Palestine, the word 'martyr' is traditionally used to mean a person killed by Israeli forces, regardless of religion.[16][11]: 216  For example, Shireen Abu Akleh was a Palestinian Christian journalist who was killed by Israeli forces, and Arabic media calls her a 'martyr'.[17] This reflects a communal belief that every Palestinian death is part of a resistance against Israeli occupation.[18] Children are likewise called martyrs, such as the children of journalist Wael Al-Dahdouh who were killed in an Israeli airstrike.[19]

The label of martyrdom is used as a form of memoralizing the dead within some narrative, such as how the victims of the 2020 Beirut explosion were called 'martyrs of corruption' as a form of protest against the government.[20]

The wide usage of 'martyr' is not restricted to Arabic. Armenian culture likewise uses the term for the victims of the Armenian genocide, who are called Holy Martyrs.[21] April 24 is Armenian Genocide Memorial Day, and also called "Armenian Martyrs Day".[22]
